host.title: Host
host.description: Hostname or IP address of the Windows host.

transport.title: Transport
transport.description: Protocol that carries the WMI queries. DCOM uses TCP 135 and a dynamic RPC port; WinRM uses HTTPS on TCP 5986.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.description: Authentication protocol for the Windows account. NTLMv2 is the only supported protocol.

username.title: Username
username.description: Windows account that reads WMI on the host, as `DOMAIN\user`, `user@domain` or a local account name.

autodetection_retry.title: Detection retry
autodetection_retry.description: How often to retry the initial connection when the job fails to start, in seconds. Zero disables retries.

timeout.title: Timeout
timeout.description: Time limit for one collection, including the connection and every enabled query, in seconds.

collectors.title: Metric groups
collectors.description: Metric groups to collect. Each enabled group runs one WMI query per collection, the memory group four and the network group two. Keep at least one group enabled.

cpu.title: CPU
cpu.description: Collect processor utilization by mode, in total and per logical processor.

memory.title: Memory
memory.description: Collect physical and available memory, commit charge, paging activity, page faults, kernel memory pools, the system cache and page lists, the usage of each paging file, and the free and standby memory of each NUMA node.

system.title: System
system.description: Collect the number of processes and threads, context switches, processor queue length and uptime.

network.title: Network
network.description: Collect traffic, packets, errors, drops, speed and output queue length per network interface, and the host's total traffic.

disk.title: Disk
disk.description: Collect available and used space per fixed drive.

tls_ca.title: TLS CA file
tls_ca.description: Path on the poller to the PEM file of the CA that issued the WinRM listener certificate. Leave empty to use the system trust store.

host.ui:help: The value identifies the job's virtual node, so changing it later creates a new node. With WinRM, it must match a name in the listener certificate.

transport.ui:help:
DCOM needs no extra Windows service: enable the built-in Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) firewall rules. The RPC traffic is encrypted.

WinRM needs an HTTPS listener with a certificate the poller trusts. It uses one fixed port, which is easier to allow through firewalls between networks.

vnode.ui:help: Leave empty and the job creates a virtual node for the Windows host, named after its computer name. To use a virtual node you manage instead, define it in `vnodes.conf` first, then enter its name here.
